To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) disentanglement can be induced by aligning right-singular vectors with the coordinate directions in the input, 2) the leading right-singlular vectors of the generator Jacobian with respect to the input correspond to paths over which disentanglement is observed, 3) a spectral regularizer based on these vectors can be used to train a generator that produces disentangled representations of the input.

(a) the leading right singular vectors of the Jacobians of a generative model are associated with directions in latent space that are locally disentangled; (b) the singular vectors are not aligned with the coordinate axes; and (c) we propose a simple, efficient regularizer that forces alignment of the singular vectors with the coordinate directions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) understanding the conditions under which GANs can be made to learn disentangled representations; (b) developing a spectral regularizer for this purpose; and (c) evaluating its performance on several datasets.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how one can find paths over which disentanglement happens, and then use that to regularize the model to learn disentanglement in a general way, for any GAN architecture.
we show that disentanglement is possible in GANs without the need of supervision and we propose a regularizer to achieve it in a completely unsuervised way.
we provide a novel and efficient regularization technique to induce disentangled representation in GANs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
disentanglement is not a property of a model, but rather a property of a path in latent space.
the latent space of a GAN is a low-rank matrix, and that disentanglement can be achieved by aligning its right-singular vectors with the coordinate directions.
, while disentanglement is a desirable property of generative models, it does not necessarily have to be explicitly learned.
